key_idea: Neighbours i,j need distance max(d_i,d_j); seating people in sorted order makes every value pay once and the maximum twice, which matches the lower bound.
sketch: The circumference is the sum over the n adjacent pairs of max(d_i,d_j). The k largest people touch at least k+1 edges, giving the lower bound sum(d) - min(d) + max(d), achieved by seating in sorted order around the circle. So answer = (sum of all but the smallest) + largest. O(n log n). Pitfalls: 64-bit sum (1e5 * 1e9), and n=2 where both arcs must be at least the larger value, which the formula already handles.
